//: Story Phase 4, chapter 18: Shark Duty. Day 7. The duty barrel is at (13,24) with Jory beside it at (12,24); the port rail sections are data (data/hazards/shark_duty.json). Ned counts from the bow (9,37). Garrick eats garlic toast at his station (11,17). On three bells the crew fall back aft (rows 13-15) and the captain fetches Squawks from his nest (12,13). The Center settles on the port rail midships (port_waterline) and the sea erupts. Damage is the variable p4_hull_damage (1-3), which the deck's props follow.

p4c4.begin.narrate: The rowboat lure worked, once. But the Revenge herself is soaked through with the Gust. She leaks it into the sea like a teabag, and leaves a trail behind her you could follow blindfolded.
The sharks follow it. Every day there are a few more.

p4c4.roster: jory: Morning, Captain. You're on the roster.
jory: Shark Duty. Everyone takes a shift. Poles, paddles, the mop, the broom, the boathook. You walk the rail and you... discourage them.
jory[annoyed]: Rap them on the nose, mostly. They hate that. They come back, but they hate it.
pete[tired]: Worst job on the ship.
captain: And why don't we just send Garrick out in the rowboat again?
jory: Asked him. Something about pressure. I stopped listening, Captain. You'll have to ask him yourself.

p4c4.roster.tutorial: Take a pole from the Shark Duty barrel next to Jory, then report to the port rail (the right-hand side of the deck).
p4c4.roster.title: Shark Duty

p4c4.pole: A barrel of Shark Duty tools: two poles, a boathook, a paddle, a mop and a broom. Every handle has a bite mark near the far end.
You pick the long pole. It has the fewest bite marks.
jory: Port rail's yours, Captain. Watch for the red marks. That's where they're coming up.

p4c4.pole.tutorial: SHARK DUTY: sharks surface along the port rail under a red marker. Walk to the rail beside it, face it and press Confirm, then strike on the green. Too slow and it takes a bite, which you'll have to patch. Arrows at the edge of the screen point to sharks you can't see.
p4c4.pole.title: Shark Duty

p4c4.rant: You lean on your pole. Below the rail the last shark of the watch swims off, sulking.
captain[annoyed]: You know what piracy was supposed to be?
captain[angry]: Merchant ships. Treasure. Cannon fire. RAIDS. A fat Spanish galleon across the Main with every sail set and a cutlass in my teeth.
captain[angry]: Not spending half the day poking sharks on the nose because they ENJOY Garrick's atmospheric catastrophe!
pete[tired]: You get used to it, Captain.
captain[tired]: I don't WANT to get used to it.
jory: Speaking of which. Come and look at the port side, Captain, while it's quiet.

p4c4.rant.tutorial: Check the port damage with Jory, by the duty barrel.
p4c4.rant.title: Shark Duty

p4c4.port_damage: jory: See that patch? That's my patch from the first attack. That one's still good.
jory: The one next to it's a patch over a bite in the patch. And that one's a patch for THAT patch.
jory[annoyed]: I've started writing on them so I know which is which.

p4c4.port_damage.caption: Chalked on the hull, in Jory's hand.

p4c4.port_damage: jory: Ned's been counting fins off the bow all morning, Captain. He's got a face on him.

p4c4.port_damage.tutorial: Check the starboard activity with Ned, the lookout (at the bow).
p4c4.port_damage.title: Shark Duty

p4c4.count: ned: Twenty to port. Give or take.
captain: Fifty. We can manage fifty.
ned[alarmed]: ...And more coming. From astern. From everywhere.
Hundreds of fins. The sea around the Queen Anne's Revenge is so thick with them it looks planted, like a field.

p4c4.count.tutorial: They're coming at both rails now, and some are coming aboard. Hold them off!
p4c4.count.title: Shark Duty

p4c4.toast: You lean on your pole, gasping, and look down the deck.
Sitting comfortably on his barrel beneath the Forecast Board, the Grand Stenchmaster is eating garlic toast.

p4c4.toast.tutorial: Get the Grand Stenchmaster to help. (He's at his station, midships.)
p4c4.toast.title: Shark Duty

p4c4.refusal: captain[angry]: Garrick. What are you eating.
garrick[happy]: Garlic toast, Captain! Want a bite?
captain[angry]: GARLIC. There are hundreds of sharks out there following your smell, and you are eating GARLIC.
garrick[businesslike]: Leadership requires energy, Captain.
captain[determined]: Put it down. Pick up a pole. Get on the rail.
garrick[neutral]: No.
The deck goes quiet. Even the sharks seem to pause.
captain[surprised]: ...No?
garrick[businesslike]: Manual shark labour is outside the responsibilities of the Grand Stenchmaster.
rook[annoyed]: THE SHARKS ARE HERE BECAUSE OF THE STENCH!
pete[annoyed]: You're the STENCHmaster!
jory[annoyed]: It's obviously a Stenchmaster problem.
garrick[offended]: I disagree. This is SHARK MANAGEMENT. That's a different department entirely.
garrick[businesslike]: My office handles odour classification. Forecasts. Frog Grog oversight. Beard inspection. And general stench ceremony.
captain[angry]: GENERAL STENCH CEREMONY IS NOT A REAL JOB.
garrick[offended]: ...How DARE you, Captain. Insulting the office. In front of the crew.
Behind him, a shark is quietly eating the rail.
captain: Then do the other thing. The rowboat. Lead them off, like last time.
garrick[nervous]: Ah. No. Can't be done, Captain.
garrick[businesslike]: The last one took preparation. Two pots of beans, a cabbage and a very long, very tense afternoon. I haven't got the pressure. Not for hundreds.

garrick[businesslike]: Anything I could manage right now would be a whisper. They wouldn't even turn round. Not with the Center aboard. It's a far stronger smell than anything I can do at short notice.
captain[resigned]: So the one man who could lead them away can't, and won't hold a pole.
garrick[proud]: I can offer moral support!
Everybody freezes.

Across the deck, the Dead Center has come up out of the main hatch, and it is rolling toward the port rail. Toward the patch. Toward the exact piece of hull the whole crew has spent the morning defending.
jory[alarmed]: Not the PATCH!
captain[determined]: Abandon duty! Everyone clear of the port rail! AFT! MOVE!

p4c4.refusal.tutorial: Abandon Shark Duty! Get Squawks from his nest (aft, beside the cabin door) and get clear of the port rail.
p4c4.refusal.title: Shark Duty

p4c4.frenzy: squawks[worried]: Bells?
captain: Bells. In the coat.
You tuck him into your coat and fall back with the crew.
The Dead Center reaches the rail. It spills over it, slow as honey, and slides down the side of the ship into the sea.
The ocean ERUPTS.
Every shark in the sea turns toward the ship at once. They come from everywhere, hundreds of them, churning the water white.
A hammerhead the size of the rowboat comes up out of the foam and slams its head into the hull. It backs off. It does it again.
Others are fighting over the planks it knocks loose.
garrick[delighted]: Fascinating. FASCINATING! Look at them, Captain! The Center's reached the water and they've gone absolutely wild for it!
garrick[businesslike]: I'd estimate the Center increases the attraction by... oh, a great deal. A factor of lots.
captain[angry]: WE ARE NOT CONDUCTING RESEARCH!
jory[alarmed]: The patch! Captain, I have to get to the patch!
captain[determined]: You'd be on the floor in three breaths. NOBODY goes near that rail till it moves.
The Center hasn't moved. Neither have the sharks. The rail is gone between the second and third cannon. Jory's patch is gone. Jory's patch for the patch is gone.
rook[alarmed]: They've had the bucket! The one that hung on the rail! They ATE the BUCKET!
You look at your ship. He's right. She is, very slightly, but definitely, smaller than she was this morning.
captain[angry]: I have fought the Royal Navy. I have fought the Spanish, the Dutch, and a Portuguese admiral with a wooden nose.
captain[angry]: I have sailed through hurricanes. I was sentenced to hang in three ports and I walked out of all of them. Thirty years of piracy, and I've kept all my fingers and most of my teeth.
captain[devastated]: And now my ship is going to be destroyed. My ship. The Queen Anne's Revenge.
captain[devastated]: Because sharks. Are attracted. To a FART.
garrick[businesslike]: To be fair, Captain, the ship hasn't ended YET.
Something large breaks off the port side and splashes into the sea.
captain[angry]: IT IS ACTIVELY ENDING.
Garrick takes out a crayon and a fresh sheet of paper, sits down on his barrel, and begins to draw.
pete[disgusted]: He's... he's drawing it.
wick[surprised]: He's drawing the sharks eating the ship. While they're eating the ship.
garrick[businesslike]: Documentation matters, Mister Wick. In a hundred years somebody will want to know exactly how this went.
garrick[proud]: 'Response: excellent.'
captain[angry]: EXCELLENT? Which part of this was EXCELLENT?
garrick[smug]: The sharks' response, Captain. Textbook.
